question: Why is isolated pure knowerhood insufficient to explain worldly cognition?
premises: In the purely isolated aspect of knowerhood there is no cognition as such.
Worldly knowerhood always involves determinate cognition.
Worldly knowerhood is therefore of a different, differentiated kind.
inference: Pure isolated knowerhood cannot account for cognition, whereas all worldly knowerhood is constituted by such differentiated cognition.
plain_english: In that isolated aspect there is no cognition at all, so what use is that isolated state? But every worldly state of being a knower is of this differentiated kind.
